newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila overnight money jumps on rate increase.
newsitem.headline: Manila overnight money jumps on rate increase.

text.p: * Volume falls to 7.026 bln from 7.517 bln pesos

Manila overnight money jumped to an average of 10.28125 percent on Friday from 10.03125 following the 0.25 percentage-point hike in the Central Bank's overnight borrowing rate to 10.25 percent, dealers said.
The Central Bank raised its rate to align it with the rising Treasury bill rates and to defend the peso which had been under attack in recent days, they said.
Banks had been buying dollars after the stock market was battered in recent days due to talk banks could be hit hard by a possible slump in the property market.
"Investors were jittery. If interest differentials do not justify the risk, they will go out," a foreign bank dealer said.
Done rates were from 10.3125 to 10.28125 percent, with 22 lenders and 19 borrowers.
In the secondary market, banks were trying to unload their old, low-interest bills ahead of the expected rise in Treasury bill rates at the auction on Monday.
"But no one wants to buy," another trader said.
A Reuters poll of seven financial institutions gave offer rates of 10.185 to 10.375 on the three-month bills; 10.50 to 10.65 on the six months; and 11.20 to 11.375 on the one-year bills.
